content: {"rules": ["Model consistently underestimates volatility and fails to capture sudden upward spikes (e.g., +5-6 EUR) when recent history shows high variance.", "Forecast exhibits a strong downward bias during periods of low or zero sentiment, often predicting flatlines while outcomes show significant range expansion.", "When sentiment shifts from 0.00 to positive values (e.g., 0.20-0.40), the model fails to adjust its trajectory upward immediately, resulting in persistent underperformance relative to true outcomes.", "Model forecasts are overly smooth and lack the mean-reversion dynamics seen in true data; it tends to extrapolate recent trends linearly rather than oscillating around a moving average.", "In high-volatility regimes (standard deviation > 3 EUR), the model's confidence interval is too narrow, leading to frequent large errors on both sides of the forecast path."]}
